# Behavioral Specification: Flash Physical Read Pipeline

## 1. Overview

This module implements the read path for the flash physical layer. It accepts flash read transactions, serves them from a small read cache when possible, or reads the flash array directly. It is responsible for:

- preserving transaction order,
- handling the optional descrambling of flash data,
- checking and reporting reliability ECC errors,
- checking and reporting integrity ECC errors,
- returning the addressed bus word, and
- invalidating cached data when stateful operations affect it.

The module assumes the response consumer always accepts a returned read response in the same cycle. It must not accept a new read transaction unless it is certain the transaction can eventually be completed in order without requiring response-side backpressure.

## 2. Reset and Initialization

After reset:

- The read cache must be disabled.
- All cache entries must be invalid.
- No read responses shall be produced.
- The module shall indicate idle.

The cache shall remain disabled until explicitly enabled by configuration. While the cache is disabled, no cache lookups or cache allocations may be performed.

The cache-enable setting may only take effect when the read pipeline is idle. If the enable value changes, new read transactions must be held off until the new value is safely captured. This prevents a read from being handled with a mix of old and new cache-enable behavior.

## 3. Read Transaction Acceptance

A read transaction is considered accepted only when a request is present and the module asserts ready in the same cycle.

Each accepted read transaction must eventually produce exactly one response. The response must contain:

- the selected bus word of the addressed flash word,
- the corresponding bus integrity information,
- an in-band error indication, and
- any out-of-band error indications applicable to the transaction.

The module must not accept a new transaction when any of the following conditions exist:

- The cache-enable value is in the process of changing.
- The flash read stage is busy and cannot accept another read.
- The internal response-ordering storage is full.
- The internal storage needed for pending read data or descrambling masks is full.
- A mask calculation for a previously accepted descrambled read is still outstanding.
- Every cache entry is currently tied to an already-accepted response and no invalid entry is available for replacement.

A transaction that is not accepted shall be ignored and may be retried later.

## 4. Read Cache Behavior

### 4.1 Cache Match

When the cache is enabled, each incoming read address is compared against the cache entries. The comparison must include the flash word address, the flash partition, and the information-partition selection.

A cache hit occurs when:

- the entry matches the transaction address and partition,
- the entry is in a valid or currently-filling state, and
- the entry does not contain a recorded error.

If the matching entry is already valid, the response may be supplied from the cache as soon as that response reaches the head of the response order.

If the matching entry is still being filled, the transaction must wait for the fill to complete before the response is returned. No new flash read shall be issued for such a transaction.

An entry that contains an error must never be used to satisfy a new read transaction. Such an entry is treated as unavailable for reuse until any response already depending on it has been delivered.

### 4.2 Cache Miss and Allocation

If the cache is enabled and a read does not match any usable entry:

- The module must allocate a cache entry for the flash word.
- A flash read must be issued for that flash word.
- The cache entry must transition to the filling state.
- When the read data completes, the entry must be updated with the de-scrambled data and its error status.

If an invalid entry exists, it should be used for allocation before reusing a valid entry.

If no invalid entry exists, a valid entry may be reused, but the module must never replace:

- an entry that is currently being filled, or
- an entry on which an already-accepted response depends.

If all available entries are busy with existing responses and no invalid entry exists, the module must stop accepting new transactions until a dependency clears.

### 4.3 Cache Disabled Mode

When the cache is disabled:

- No cache match shall be reported.
- No cache entry shall be allocated.
- Every accepted read transaction must cause a flash read.
- The returned data shall be sent directly through the read pipeline.

### 4.4 Invalidation on Program and Erase

The module observes stateful-operation sideband indications for programming, page erase, and bank erase.

- A bank erase must invalidate all valid cache entries.
- A page erase must invalidate valid cache entries for flash words within the erased page.
- A program operation must invalidate valid cache entries for the flash word being programmed.

Invalidated entries must not be used for later reads. If an invalidated entry already has a pending response, the entry must remain intact until that response is delivered, and only then become reusable.

Entries currently being filled shall not be invalidated by stateful-operation sideband indications.

## 5. Flash Read Stage

When a cache miss is accepted, the module must issue a flash read request for the addressed flash word.

Only one flash read may be outstanding at a time. A new flash read may begin only when the current flash read is complete and the pipeline resources are available.

The module must keep track of the following attributes for the outstanding flash read:

- the flash word address,
- whether the location must be descrambled, and
- whether reliability ECC and integrity checking are enabled.

When the flash read data is returned, the module must determine:

- whether the returned flash word is in the erased state,
- whether the reliability ECC check detected a correctable error,
- whether the reliability ECC check detected an uncorrectable error, and
- whether the data can be forwarded directly or must wait for descrambling.

## 6. Descrambling

### 6.1 Mask Calculation

If the current read transaction requires descrambling, the module must request a mask calculation as soon as the flash read request has been accepted.

The mask calculation is address-based and is performed in parallel with the flash read.

While the mask calculation is outstanding, the module must not accept any new read transaction.

### 6.2 Data Fill and Descramble Decision

When the flash read returns, the module must decide whether descrambling is actually required.

If the data is all ones, the location is considered erased. In this case:

- descrambling must be skipped,
- the computed mask, once available, must be discarded, and
- the erased data pattern shall be used as the read data.

If the data is not erased and descrambling is enabled:

- the read data must be held until the mask is available,
- a descramble operation must be requested,
- the data presented to the descrambler must be the raw data word combined with the computed mask according to the scrambling scheme,
- the final data must be formed by combining the descrambler output with the same mask.

If descrambling is not enabled:

- no descramble operation shall be requested,
- the data may be forwarded directly if no older transaction is still ahead of it in the pipeline,
- otherwise, the data must be queued so that transaction order is preserved.

### 6.3 Ordering with Descramble

The module must never allow a newer non-descrambled read to overtake an older read that is still waiting for descrambling.

When a read has a corresponding mask, the queued read data and mask must be consumed together, in the same order as the corresponding transactions. A directly forwarded response may be generated before its queued data and mask are consumed.

## 7. Response Generation

### 7.1 Response Order

The module must preserve the order of accepted read transactions. A read transaction that hits a valid cache entry must not be returned before any older accepted transaction has been returned.

A response is produced when both of the following are true:

- the transaction is at the head of the response order, and
- the required data is available, either from the cache, from the flash read stage, or from the descrambling stage.

The data-valid output shall be asserted for a single cycle for each response.

### 7.2 Data Selection

If the flash word is wider than the bus word, the module must select the bus word corresponding to the address of the original read transaction.

The returned data must be accompanied by the required bus integrity encoding computed over the selected bus word.

If the response has an in-band error, the returned data word shall be all ones, but the bus integrity encoding must still be generated consistently with that all-ones word.

### 7.3 Response from Cache

When a response is served from a valid cache entry:

- The data shall be the cached de-scrambled flash word.
- The transaction’s integrity-check enable setting must still be applied to the cached data.
- Any error that was recorded when the flash word was fetched must be reported as an in-band error.

## 8. Error Reporting

### 8.1 Reliability ECC

Reliability ECC checking is performed only when the transaction has ECC checking enabled for the addressed location.

If a single-bit error is detected:

- the data shall be corrected before being stored or returned,
- a correctable-error output shall be asserted, and
- no in-band error shall be reported for that transaction.

If a multi-bit error is detected:

- the corrected result may still be passed through the pipeline, but the transaction must be marked as erroneous,
- an in-band error must be reported when the response is returned,
- an out-of-band uncorrectable reliability error must be asserted, and
- the addressed flash word must be reported with the error.

If ECC is disabled, no reliability ECC correction or error reporting shall be performed.

The address reported with a reliability ECC error must be the flash-word address of the read that detected the error.

### 8.2 Integrity ECC

Integrity checking is performed when the transaction has integrity checking enabled.

The integrity ECC must be checked against the final de-scrambled data before it is returned.

If the integrity check fails:

- an in-band error must be asserted with the response,
- an out-of-band integrity error must be asserted, and
- the returned data must be all ones.

### 8.3 Stored Cache Errors

If a valid cache entry was filled with an uncorrectable reliability error, any later response served from that entry must assert an in-band error.

Such an entry must not be used to satisfy new read matches, but it must be retained until any response already waiting on it has been delivered.

### 8.4 Catastrophic Error Indication

If the module receives a catastrophic arbitration error indication, the in-band error output must be asserted.

### 8.5 Internal Queue Errors

If any internal storage structure reports an integrity failure, the module must assert its queue-error output.

## 9. Idle Indication

The module shall indicate that the read pipeline is idle when there are no accepted read transactions with a response still pending.

The idle indication shall be deasserted as soon as an accepted transaction is waiting for a response and shall remain deasserted until that response has been returned.

The idle indication may be used to allow configuration changes, such as enabling or disabling the read cache, to take effect safely.

# Flash Physical Read Module Specification

## 1. Overview

The module implements the read datapath between a flash memory and the bus-facing consumer. It accepts read transactions, fetches the requested flash words, optionally descrambles them, performs integrity and ECC checking, caches recently read data, and returns bus-width words in order.

The module is designed so that responses are always accepted by the downstream consumer. It may backpressure new read requests, but once a response is presented it must be consumed without additional backpressure.

## 2. Read Transaction Handling

### 2.1 Request Acceptance

A read transaction is accepted only when the module indicates it is ready. Each accepted transaction must eventually produce exactly one response.

The module must not accept a new transaction when:

- internal response-ordering storage has no space for another transaction;
- the read datapath staging resources are full;
- a required flash read cannot be started because the flash read stage is busy;
- a descrambling mask calculation is still outstanding; or
- cache replacement cannot be performed because all eligible cache entries are still needed by earlier outstanding transactions.

A transaction that hits in the read cache may be accepted without starting a flash read, but it must still wait behind earlier accepted transactions so that responses remain ordered.

### 2.2 Response Ordering

Responses must be returned in the same order as the corresponding read transactions were accepted. A later cache hit must not jump ahead of an earlier transaction that is still waiting for a flash read or descrambling operation to complete.

The module must preserve this ordering even when some transactions are served from flash and others are served directly from the cache.

## 3. Read Buffer / Cache Behavior

The module maintains a small set of read-buffer entries. Each entry stores one complete flash word, along with the address, partition and information-partition attributes, validity state, and any error status associated with that word.

### 3.1 Caching Enabled

When caching is enabled:

- A read request that matches a valid cache entry, or an entry that is currently being fetched from flash, must not issue a new flash read.
- A request that does not match any cache entry must allocate a cache entry and start a flash read.
- Replacement must prefer invalid entries first. If no invalid entry exists, it must select a valid entry that is not still needed by an older outstanding response.
- An entry that is currently being fetched must never be replaced.
- A cache entry that contains an unrecoverable error must not be used to satisfy subsequent read hits once all older responses waiting on that entry have been delivered.

### 3.2 Caching Disabled

When caching is disabled, every read transaction must be fetched from flash memory. No cache lookup, allocation, or update is performed.

### 3.3 Enabling and Disabling the Cache

The cache-enable setting may change only when the read pipeline has no outstanding responses. While the setting is transitioning, the module must not accept new read transactions. This ensures that all older transactions are handled consistently with the cache configuration that was active when they were accepted.

## 4. Flash Read Behavior

For a read transaction that requires a flash access, the module must:

- issue a read request to the flash memory for the addressed flash word;
- retain the transaction’s attributes, including address, descrambling requirement, and ECC/integrity enable;
- wait for the flash read to complete before returning data;
- not start another flash read until the current one has completed or is completing.

After the flash read completes, the data may either be forwarded directly toward the response path or pass through internal staging storage. The choice must preserve response ordering and must not cause a later transaction to overtake an earlier one.

## 5. Scrambling and Descrambling

For a read transaction that requires descrambling:

- The module must request mask/tweak calculation for the addressed flash word in parallel with the flash read.
- It must not accept another read transaction while the mask calculation is still outstanding.
- When both the flash read data and the calculated mask are available, the module must send the data through the descrambling stage.
- The descrambled result must be used as the returned data.

If the flash word contains the erased value, i.e. all bits are one, descrambling is not required even if the transaction normally requires it. The mask calculation result must be discarded, and the erased data value is returned directly.

If a read transaction does not require descrambling, the flash data must bypass the descrambling stage.

## 6. Error Detection and Reporting

### 6.1 Reliability ECC

When reliability ECC checking is enabled for a transaction, the module must check the flash word as it is read from flash.

- A single-bit error must be corrected. The corrected data must be used for the response.
- A single-bit error must be reported as a correctable error indication, together with the address of the flash word in which the error occurred.
- A multi-bit, uncorrectable error must be reported as an in-band data error for the affected response and as an out-of-band reliability ECC error.
- When reliability ECC checking is disabled, raw flash data must be returned without correction or ECC error reporting.

### 6.2 Integrity / ICV Check

When integrity checking is enabled for a transaction, the module must verify the integrity field carried with the descrambled or cached data.

- If the integrity check fails, the response must carry an in-band data error.
- The module must also assert an out-of-band integrity error indication.
- This check must be performed for responses served from flash and for responses served from the read cache.

### 6.3 Data Error Responses

When a read response has an unrecoverable reliability ECC error, an integrity error, a cached error status, or a catastrophic arbitration error indication, the module must mark the response as an error.

When an in-band error is asserted, the returned data word must be all ones.

### 6.4 Internal Storage Errors

The module must detect integrity failures in its internal ordering and staging storage. If such a failure occurs, it must assert a dedicated internal error indication.

### 6.5 Catastrophic Arbitration Error

If a catastrophic arbitration error indication is presented to the module, the module must assert its in-band data error indication.

## 7. Response Generation

For every accepted read transaction, the module must return exactly one bus-width data word.

The correct bus word within the flash word must be selected using the low-order address offset of the original read request. If the flash word width is equal to the bus word width, no selection is needed.

The returned data word must be the appropriate value from:

- the descrambled flash read result,
- the directly forwarded raw flash read result, or
- a valid read-buffer entry.

The module must also provide the required bus integrity metadata with the returned data word.

The module must indicate when a response is valid and must not rely on the consumer to backpressure the response. It must also provide an idle indication that is asserted when no read responses are outstanding.

## 8. Coherence with Program and Erase

The module must observe program and erase activity so that the read cache does not return stale data after flash contents are modified.

- A program operation that targets the same flash word as a valid cache entry must invalidate that entry.
- A page erase operation that targets the same page as a valid cache entry must invalidate all matching cache entries in that page.
- A bank erase operation must invalidate all cache entries.

For program and page erase, the partition and information-partition attributes of the cache entry must match the operation. A program or erase in one partition must not invalidate a cache entry for a different partition.

These invalidations ensure that subsequent reads after a program or erase obtain fresh data from flash rather than obsolete cached data.

## 9. Reset and Initial State

After reset, the module must:

- clear all read-buffer entries;
- disable caching;
- have no outstanding responses; and
- assert its idle indication.

# Flash Physical Read Pipeline Specification

## 1. Overview

This module implements the flash read datapath. It accepts read requests from the flash controller/arbitration logic, checks a small read-buffer cache, issues reads to the flash memory when necessary, optionally descrambles the returned data, performs ECC and integrity checking, and returns ordered, bus-width read data to the requester.

A flash word may be wider than the bus word returned to the requester. The module therefore returns the selected bus word from the flash word, while retaining the full flash word in its cache for subsequent accesses that hit the same flash word.

The response side of this module is not backpressured. When a response is presented, it must be consumed in the same cycle. The module assumes the upstream consumer always accepts responses and that no response-ready slow-down exists.

## 2. Request Acceptance and Ordering

Read requests are accepted only when the module can guarantee that they can eventually be completed and that responses can be returned in the same order in which the requests were accepted.

An accepted request must eventually produce exactly one response. The module shall maintain the ordering of all accepted read requests. A read that hits in the cache may be answered without accessing flash. A read that misses the cache must be answered after the flash read and any descrambling work is complete.

The module must not accept a new request when:

- The response-ordering path is full.
- The read-datapath staging area for data or descrambling masks is full.
- A flash read is already in progress and the new request would require another flash read.
- A mask calculation for an earlier descrambling read is still outstanding.
- The cache is currently changing between enabled and disabled.
- Every cache entry has an outstanding dependency and allocation would be required.

If a request hits a cache entry that is currently being filled, the request does not need to start a new flash read. It is accepted using only the response-ordering capacity and is answered once the cache fill completes.

## 3. Read Buffer Cache

The module maintains a small set of read buffer entries. Each entry stores:

- The flash-word address.
- The partition and information-type selection.
- The data read from flash, before or after descrambling as applicable.
- Error status associated with that data.
- A state indicating whether the entry is invalid, valid, or currently being filled.

### 3.1 Hit Behavior

A read request hits the cache when:

- The cache is enabled.
- The request address matches the flash-word address of a valid or in-progress entry.
- The partition and information-type selection match.
- The entry does not have a recorded error.

A request that hits a valid entry is answered from that entry when it reaches the head of the response order.

A request that hits an in-progress entry waits for that entry to complete and then answers from the completed entry.

A valid entry with a recorded error shall not be treated as a hit. A read to that address must miss and be fetched from flash again.

### 3.2 Allocation and Replacement

When a request misses the cache and the cache is enabled, the module must allocate a cache entry.

An invalid entry shall be selected first. If no invalid entry exists, a valid entry may be selected. Entries that are currently being filled must never be replaced. Entries that still have outstanding responses depending on them must not be replaced.

If all valid entries currently have outstanding dependencies, the module must wait before allocating and must backpressure new requests that would require allocation.

A valid entry that has a recorded error and no longer has any outstanding response depending on it may be treated as available for reuse.

### 3.3 Buffer Invalidation on Program and Erase

Program and erase operations are observed as sideband operations. They do not generate read responses. They are only expected when the read pipeline is idle.

The module must invalidate cache entries as follows:

- A program operation targeting the same flash word as a valid entry invalidates that entry.
- A page erase operation targeting a page containing valid entries invalidates all valid entries in that page.
- A bank erase operation invalidates all valid entries.

Entries that are currently being filled must not be invalidated by program or erase operations.

### 3.4 Cache Enable

When the cache is disabled, no cache lookups or allocations are performed. Every accepted read is treated as a miss and must be fetched from flash.

The cache enable state may change only when the read pipeline is idle. If a new request arrives while an enable-state change is settling, the module must backpressure that request until the state is stable.

## 4. Flash Read Behavior

A flash read is started only for requests that miss the cache or for all requests when the cache is disabled.

The module can have only one flash read outstanding at a time. While a flash read is in progress, a new request that requires a flash read must be held. A read that completes in the same cycle may allow a subsequent read to begin in that cycle.

When a flash read is started, the module must remember the attributes of that transaction for use when the data returns, including:

- The flash-word address.
- Whether the address is scrambled and therefore requires descrambling.
- Whether ECC checking is enabled for this read.

If the request requires descrambling, mask calculation is started in parallel with the flash access. The mask calculation may finish before or after the flash data returns. While this mask calculation is outstanding, the module must not accept another request.

The module must not start a flash read if there is no space in the internal data staging or mask staging resources, because the returned read data must be captured without loss.

## 5. Erased Flash Word Handling

When flash data returns, the module must detect the erased state, defined as all bits of the full flash word being 1.

If the read location was marked as scrambled but the data is erased, the data does not need to be descrambled. The computed mask is no longer needed and shall be discarded once it is ready. The erased data is treated as plaintext.

If the read location was not marked as scrambled, no descrambling is performed regardless of the erased state.

## 6. Descrambling and Data Forwarding

For a non-erased read that requires descrambling, the module must wait until both the flash data and the computed mask are available. It then requests descrambling and returns the descrambled result.

For a read that does not require descrambling, the data may be forwarded directly once the flash read completes, provided there are no earlier data items still waiting in the staging path. If earlier items exist, the data must be queued behind them so that response order is preserved.

No data item shall pass another data item in the pipeline. All responses must be presented in request order.

## 7. Reliability ECC Checking

When ECC checking is enabled for a read transaction, the full flash word is checked against the reliability ECC code on return from flash.

- A single-bit error must be corrected. The corrected data is used. The module shall assert an out-of-band single-bit error indication and provide the address of the flash word where the error occurred.
- A multi-bit error is uncorrectable. The module shall assert an in-band data error and an out-of-band reliability error. It must still return data, using the ECC-corrected result even though that result is not trustworthy. This data may be stored in the cache and marked as erroneous.

When ECC checking is disabled, no reliability ECC correction or error reporting is performed and the raw flash data is used.

Reliability ECC error indications are mutually exclusive: a given read cannot be reported as both a single-bit and a multi-bit error.

## 8. Integrity Checking

The module must check the plaintext integrity tag of the response data when integrity checking is enabled for that transaction.

This integrity check applies regardless of whether the response comes from the flash read path, the descrambling path, or the cache.

If the integrity check fails, the module must:

- Assert an in-band data error.
- Assert an out-of-band integrity error.
- Present an all-ones data word to the requester.

If a response comes from a cache entry that has a stored reliability error, the module must also assert an in-band data error for that response.

## 9. Response Generation

Responses are presented in the exact order in which requests were accepted. Each accepted request produces exactly one response.

The response data is the selected bus word from the returned flash word. The selection is based on the bus-word offset recorded when the request was accepted.

The response data must include the bus-integrity encoding required by the bus interface.

When any error applies to the response, including reliability multi-bit errors, integrity-check failures, stored cache errors, or an external catastrophic arbitration error, the data word presented to the requester must be all ones, and the data-error indication must be asserted.

A response shall be presented only when the response data and its error status are known and valid.

## 10. Error and Fault Indications

The module provides separate indications for recoverable single-bit reliability errors, uncorrectable reliability errors, and integrity errors.

A catastrophic external arbitration error shall force the data-error status active. If a valid response is presented at the same time, that response is marked with an error.

If any internal FIFO or storage element detects an integrity/fault condition, the module shall assert a fault indication.

## 11. Idle Indication

The module shall assert its idle indication when there are no accepted requests still waiting in the response-ordering path. In this state, no response is pending and no response-order dependency remains.

Idle is the safe state for changing the cache enable setting and for accepting program/erase cache-maintenance sideband operations.

The idle indication is local to the read pipeline and does not necessarily indicate that the flash memory itself is idle.
